sentences.text:
Applicant :- Gufan Ahmad
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjai Kumar Pandey,Manisha Trivedi,Rahul Srivastava,Ratnesh Tr Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.
Heard Shri Rahul Srivastava, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Gufan Ahmad for grant of bail, in Case Crime No.146 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. & 3/4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and 3(2)5 of the S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Kotwali Akbarpur, District Ambedkar Nagar, during trial.

Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that all the witnesses of fact have been examined in this case and the F.I.R. as well as the statement of two victims recorded in this case before the investigating officer under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and before the Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and before the trial court would reflect that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

It is further submitted that conjoint reading of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded before the Gufan Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104403835/
1 investigating officer and before the Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C. would reveal that one of the victim was a consenting party as she had herself accompanied the applicant with her younger sister and she was never enticed away, however, she under the influence of her family members has given the statement before the Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as during the course of trial as prosecution witness.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that there are material contradictions in the statement of the prosecutrix/victims recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. as well as recorded before the trial court as P.W.-1 and P.W.-2.

While referring to the statement given by one of the victim to the Doctor while under examination, it is submitted that the victim, who is alleging commission of rape, has informed the Doctor that she wants to go with the applicant and it clearly suggests that the applicant and the prosecutrix was in love with each other.

It further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix at the date and time of the incident, who has alleged commission of rape, has been assessed as 14-16 years through the ossification process while another prosecutrix have not alleged any allegation of rape and has also refused to undergo any medical examination and as per her educational credentials, date of birth of the victim alleging rape is 01.01.2005, however, no source has been disclosed by any official/principle of the school as to on what basis this date of birth has been recorded in the school record and having regard to the two years variables either side, the age of the prosecutrix determined through ossification process,
victim alleging rape was major and no abnormality or any injury has been found on her person while under medical examination.
It is next submitted that applicant is in jail in this case since 07.04.2021 and he is not having any criminal history, charge-sheet in this case has already been submitted and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail the applicant may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and having regard to the material/evidence available against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail, but could not controvert the other factual submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the applicant was not named in the F.I.R. On 03.04.2021 the prosecutrix is shown to have been recovered and her statement has been recorded before the investigating officer under Section 161 Cr.P.C., wherein she stated that for the last two years, she was on talking terms with the applicant.

It was on 01.04.2021 the applicant had called her to Jogapur and on this pretext she by telling her mother that she is feeling pain in her stomach and going to ease herself had fled away from the house with her younger sister and she was taken by the applicant to a room thereafter he left the house.

Thus no allegation of rape has been levelled by the prosecutrix alleging rape against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. after her alleged abduction, however,
in reply to question asked by the investigating officer, as to whether sexual relations were established by the applicant, the prosecutrix had replied that when the applicant used to come to her Gufan Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104403835/
2 house, they have cohabited.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has improved her version and had imputed allegation of rape on her by the applicant.
As allegation of rape has been levelled by her younger sister.

It has been vehemently submitted on behalf of the applicant that the factum of rape has not been established by any medical evidence and the age of the prosecutrix is such where she can take decisions and having regard to the two years variable either side in the age, which determined through ossification process, the prosecutrix was of the age, where she can take decisions, therefore,
no offence has been committed by the applicant as the prosecutrix alleging rape was a consenting party and she was in love with the applicant.
Charge-sheet in this case has already been filed.
Applicant is in jail in this case since 07.04.2021 without any previous criminal history.
The presence of the applicant could be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

Having regard to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

Let the accused/applicant- Gufan Ahmad involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) If the investigation of the case is still pending, the applicant shall remain present before the investigating officer as and when required and shall co-operate in the investigation without any excuse.
(ii) The applicant shall not attempt to make contact with the prosecutrix either directly or indirectly or through any social platform or with any of the prosecution witnesses and the violation of these conditions alone shall be a sufficient ground for the trial court to cancel the facility of bail granted by this Court.
(iii) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(iv) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(v) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
